I've computed all the answers and saved them to `answer.json`. The script that calculated them also wrote the file, so I didn't run a separate check afterwards.

| Item | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Top Q3 segment | enterprise, 346,097,785 KRW |
| b. Customers with paid Q3 orders | 249 |
| c. Top Q3 category | svc, 280,383,280 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the most Q3 refunds | u74@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid Q3 orders | 240 |
| g. Average net sales per paid Q3 order | 727,278 KRW |
| h. Growth from August to September | 14.3% |

How the data was handled:
- **Same person:** 300 customer accounts share 250 distinct emails. For b, e and f I counted each email as one customer. Email case and spacing didn't matter here: lowercasing and trimming gave the same 250 emails.
- **Segment:** each sale is counted under the segment on the account that placed it. If one person has accounts in different segments, their sales are split across those segments.
- **Refunds:** I only counted refunds on paid orders, using the same Korean-time (UTC+9) date as the order. Every refund row matches an existing order line, and no refund is larger than the quantity sold.
- **Order count for g:** the average divides by the number of paid Q3 orders, even if an order had no line items.
